vivekananda.oneLineEn: Neo-Vedānta figure and transmitter of modern Indian religious thought.

voltaire.oneLineEn: Enlightenment champion of tolerance, reason, and anti-clerical polemic; after Locke, in tension with Rousseau.

wang-fu.oneLineEn: Eastern Han political essayist who, in Discourses of a Recluse, criticized politics and literati ethos.

wasil-ibn-ata.oneLineEn: Early Muʿtazilī founder opening kalām splits via rational theology, free will, and intermediate position.

wilhelm-windelband.oneLineEn: Value philosophy and cultural-science method; source of Southwest neo-Kantianism.

wonhyo.oneLineEn: Korean Buddhist figure uniting diverse doctrines via harmony of disputes (hwajaeng).

wu-cheng.oneLineEn: Yuan Neo-Confucian classicist reconciling Zhu and Lu and reorganizing classical studies.
keywordsEn: Collected Sayings on the Record of Rites

wu-qi.oneLineEn: Warring States military reformer combining Military school practice with Legalist institutional color.

wu-yubi.oneLineEn: Early Ming Neo-Confucian whose Kangzhai school and reverent practice influenced Chen Xianzhang.

xiang-xiu.oneLineEn: Wei-Jin xuanxue figure known for Zhuangzi commentary and nature-vs-ritual-teaching debate.
keywordsEn: Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove
nature and the teaching of names

xu-gan.oneLineEn: Late Eastern Han Jian'an thinker who, in Zhonglun, treated governance, self-cultivation, and names-realities.

xue-xuan.oneLineEn: Ming Neo-Confucian of the Hedong school stressing return to nature and earnest practice.

xun-yue.oneLineEn: Late Eastern Han historian-essayist known for Extended Reflections and Han Annals.

yan-ying.oneLineEn: Spring and Autumn Qi statesman known for frugality, wit, and remonstrance.

yang-xiong.oneLineEn: Late Western Han thinker-writer known for Model Sayings and Supreme Mystery as classic-imitating works.

yang-zhu.oneLineEn: Warring States figure whose 'for myself' and 'valuing the self' became a foil between Confucians and Mohists.

yeshayahu-leibowitz.oneLineEn: Israeli Jewish thinker holding faith as obedience to commandments, with sharp public criticism.

yi-ik.oneLineEn: Key Korean silhak figure linking Toegye Zhu Xi learning to social statecraft problems.

zhongchang-tong.oneLineEn: Late Han political essayist who, in Frank Words, voiced institutional critique and literati independence.

zigong.oneLineEn: Disciple of Confucius known for speech, government affairs, and diplomacy.

zou-yan.oneLineEn: Warring States Yin-Yang school figure known for five-virtues succession and Great Nine Continents.

song-xing.oneLineEn: Warring States Jixia figure often paired with Yin Wen; urged restraint of desire and non-contention.

xu-xing.oneLineEn: Warring States Agriculturalist known from Mencius for the tilling-together thesis.

yin-wen.oneLineEn: Warring States Jixia figure linked to names-realities, forms-names, and the Yin Wenzi tradition.
